result.text: The contracting authority wishes to acquire a modern and fully integrated Meter & Master Data Management system (MMDM system), designed for the efficient handling and administration of meter data from both current and future metering points, as well as market communication with Energinet's DataHub. The solution must be delivered as Software as a Service (SaaS). The tendered contract includes the acquisition, implementation, operation and maintenance of the MMDM system. The requested MMDM system includes: Automated data collection, advanced analysis tools, real-time reporting, and an intuitive and user-friendly interface. Fully integrated functionality with external systems such as ERP, SCADA and CRM/fleet management, with a focus on high data integrity, data security and compliance with applicable IT and data protection regulations. A robust and scalable architecture that ensures precise, reliable and stable handling of meter data - even under maximum load. A maintenance-friendly solution with high performance and flexibility in relation to future upgrades and expansions. In relation to the procurement, a consultation of documents for the tender material is being carried out on an ongoing basis.

parts.source: Ordregiver ønsker at anskaffe et moderne og fuldt integreret Meter & Master Data Management system (MMDM-system), designet til effektiv håndtering og administration af målerdata fra både nuværende og fremtidige målepunkter, samt markedkommunikation med Energinets DataHub. Løsningen skal leveres som Software as a Service (SaaS). Den udbudte kontrakt omfatter anskaffelse, implementering, drift og vedligeholdelse af MMDM-systemet. Det efterspurgte MMDM-system omfatter: Automatiseret dataindsamling, avancerede analyseværktøjer, realtidsrapportering samt en intuitiv og brugervenlig grænseflade. Fuld integreret funktionalitet med eksterne systemer som ERP, SCADA og CRM/flådestyring, med fokus på høj dataintegritet, datasikkerhed og overholdelse af gældende IT- og databeskyttelsesregler. En robust og skalerbar arkitektur, der sikrer præcis, pålidelig og stabil håndtering af målerdata- også under maksimal belastning. En vedligeholdelsesvenlig løsning med høj ydeevne og fleksibilitet i forhold til fremtidige opgraderinger og udvidelser. I relation til indkøbet gennemføres der løbende en høring af dokumenter til udbudsmaterialet.

result.text: Background and problem statement: DEHSt has been operating end-to-end digitised specialist procedures for approximately 20 years. Central components of the IT landscape used by DEHSt are in a phase of renewal. The number of software artefacts to be developed by DEHSt is continuously increasing – as a result, schedules are constantly becoming tighter and the parallelisation and complexity are increasing. Furthermore, several legacy systems must be completely replaced. To remedy this, DEHSt has developed a software development kit (SDK) consisting of software and comprehensive documentation, for example for commissioning a test and integration environment. The aim of the SDK is, on the one hand, to carry out a technological renewal and, on the other hand, to significantly increase development speed while simultaneously maintaining standards. The SDK provides documentation, software libraries, several independent services for the centralised control (workflow control) of the specialist applications, as well as a base application and an example application that integrate into DEHSt's existing software and process landscape (e.g. addressing existing central services, the so-called "DEHSt platform"). The SDK and the DEHSt platform rely on a separation of frontend (AngularJS, NgRx, Material), backend (Spring-Boot), distributed web services and a build pipeline in GitLab, as well as scalable container-based operation (Docker images on RedHat OKD). . Aim and subject matter of the project: This procurement measure tenders a framework agreement with a term of 4 years. The framework agreement may be extended twice, by one year each time. The project is intended to encompass the development and maintenance of the entire software development kit (SDK) as well as the development of specialist applications built upon it. We distinguish between three related but parallel task areas: 1) Lot 1: SDK maintenance and management 2) Lot 2: New development of specialist applications 3) Lot 3: Migration and replacement of legacy systems For the SDK team, the goal is to increase the benefit for administrative staff, but equally to positively influence the development duration of the developer teams. For the developer teams, a goal must be to develop a high-quality application in the shortest possible time based on a detailed specification. Lot LOT-0001: Development and maintenance of the DEHSt software development kit for creating specialist applications for DEHSt enforcement procedures (Lot 1). Lot 1: SDK maintenance and management . According to current planning status, the contracting authority intends to commission tasks of up to 2.560 person days (PD) in the first four years. Subject to possible changes in the legal situation regarding European and national emissions trading, the contracting authority expects that at least 50% of the upper limit for person days stated here will be commissioned. Should the contract be extended by one year each time, the contracting authority expects tasks amounting to 640 PD per extension (up to 25% of the original scope). For the purpose of approximate capacity planning, we envisage a demand of approximately 960 PD in the first year and an average of 500 PD per subsequent year. It is assumed that the workload can be distributed relatively evenly across the months so that a constant utilisation of a development team can be achieved. Lot LOT-0002: Development and maintenance of specialist applications for DEHSt enforcement procedures based on the DEHSt software development kit with a focus on new developments (Lot 2). Lot 2: New development of specialist applications . According to current planning status, the contracting authority intends to commission tasks of up to 3.056 person days (PD) in the first four years. Subject to possible changes in the legal situation regarding European and national emissions trading, the contracting authority expects that at least 50% of the upper limit for person days stated here will be commissioned. Should the contract be extended by one year each time, the contracting authority expects tasks amounting to 764 PD per extension (up to 25% of the original scope). For the purpose of approximate capacity planning, we generally envisage a demand of 500 PD per year, but in each case in 2028 and 2029 an increased demand of approximately 1.000 PD. Utilisation over the course of the year can vary greatly. The provision of the specialist applications must in the vast majority of cases take place by fixed statutory deadlines. As a result, several development projects must be processed in parallel. This is accompanied by an increased personnel requirement that must be covered by the contractor (e.g. two to four development resources work on a specialist application, up to four specialist application projects must be processed simultaneously). Unfortunately, the statutory deadlines can generally not be influenced by the contracting authority. Lot LOT-0003: Development and maintenance of specialist applications for DEHSt enforcement procedures based on the DEHSt software development kit with a focus on migration of existing specialist applications (Lot 3). Lot 3: Migration and replacement of legacy systems . According to current planning status, the contracting authority intends to commission tasks of up to 4.472 (person days) PD in the first four years. Subject to possible changes in the legal situation regarding European and national emissions trading, the contracting authority expects that at least 50% of the upper limit for person days stated here will be commissioned. Should the contract be extended by one year each time, the contracting authority expects tasks amounting to 1.118 PD per extension (up to 25% of the original scope).

parts.source: Hintergrund und Problemstellung: Die DEHSt betreibt seit ca. 20 Jahren Ende-zu-Ende digitalisierte Fachverfahren. Zentrale Komponenten der eingesetzten IT-Landschaft der DEHSt befinden sich in einer Phase der Erneuerung. Die Anzahl der von der DEHSt zu entwickelnden Softwareartefakte wächst kontinuierlich an – Zeitpläne werden dadurch stetig enger und die Parallelisierung und Komplexität nimmt zu. Mehrere Altsysteme müssen zudem vollständig abgelöst werden. Um Abhilfe zu schaffen, hat die DEHSt ein Software-Development-Kit (SDK) entwickelt, das aus Software und einer umfangreichen Dokumentation etwa für die Inbetriebnahme einer Test- und Integrationsumgebung besteht. Ziel des SDK ist dabei einerseits eine technologische Erneuerung durchzuführen, andererseits die Entwicklungsgeschwindigkeit deutlich zu erhöhen bei gleichzeitiger Wahrung von Standards. Das SDK stellt dabei Dokumentation, Software-Bibliotheken, mehrere eigenständige Dienste für die zentralisierte Steuerung (Workflowsteuerung) der Fachanwendungen sowie eine Basis- und eine Beispielanwendung bereit, die sich in die bestehende Software- und Prozesslandschaft der DEHSt integriert (also etwa bestehende Zentrale Dienste anspricht, die sog. „DEHSt-Plattform“). Das SDK und die DEHSt-Plattform setzen auf eine Trennung von Frontend (AngularJS, NgRx, Material), Backend (Spring-Boot), verteilten Webservices und einer Build-Strecke in GitLab sowie einem skalierbaren Betrieb auf Containern-Basis (Docker Images auf RedHat OKD). . Ziel und Gegenstand des Projektes: Mit dieser Beschaffungsmaßnahme wird eine Rahmenvereinbarung ausgeschrieben, die eine Laufzeit von 4 Jahren umfasst. Die Rahmenvereinbarung kann zweimal um je ein Jahr verlängert werden. Das Projekt soll die Entwicklung und Pflege des gesamten Software Development Kits (SDK) sowie die Entwicklung von darauf aufbauenden Fachanwendungen umfassen. Dabei unterscheiden wir zwischen drei verwandten aber parallelen Aufgabenbereichen: 1) Los 1: SDK-Wartung und -Management 2) Los 2: Neuentwicklung von Fachanwendungen 3) Los 3: Migration und Ablösung von Altsystemen Für das SDK-Team gilt das Ziel, den Nutzen für die Sachbearbeitung zu Erhöhen aber genauso, die Entwicklungsdauer der Entwicklerteams positiv zu beeinflussen. Für die Entwicklerteams muss es ein Ziel sein, basierend auf einer ausgearbeiteten Spezifikation, eine qualitativ hochwertige Anwendung in möglichst geringer Zeit zu entwickeln. Lot LOT-0001: Entwicklung und Wartung des DEHSt-Software-Development Kits zur Erstellung von Fachanwendungen für Vollzugsverfahren der DEHSt (Los 1). Los 1: SDK-Wartung und -Management . Nach dem aktuellen Planungsstand beabsichtigt der Auftraggeber in den ersten vier Jah-ren Aufgaben mit bis zu 2.560 Personentage (PT) zu beauftragen. Vorbehaltlich von möglichen Änderungen der Gesetzeslage rund um den europäischen und den nationalen Emis-sionshandel erwartet der Auftraggeber, dass mindestens 50% der hier genannten Obergrenze für Personentage beauftragt werden wird. Sollte der Vertrag um jeweils ein Jahr verlängert werden, erwartet der Auftraggeber Aufga-ben in der Höhe von 640 PT je Verlängerung (bis zu 25% des ursprünglichen Umfangs). Zum Zwecke einer ungefähren Kapazitätsplanung sehen wir in etwa einen Bedarf von 960 PT im ersten Jahr und durchschnittlich 500 PT je Folgejahr. Es wird davon ausgegangen, dass die Arbeitslast relativ gleichmäßig über die Monate verteilt werden kann, sodass eine konstante Auslastung eines Entwicklungsteams erreicht werden kann. Lot LOT-0002: Entwicklung und Wartung von Fachanwendungen für Vollzugsverfahren der DEHSt auf Basis des DEHSt-Software-Development Kits mit dem Schwerpunkt auf Neuentwicklungen (Los 2). Los 2: Neuentwicklung von Fachanwendungen . Nach dem aktuellen Planungsstand beabsichtigt der Auftraggeber in den ersten vier Jahren Aufgaben mit bis zu 3.056 Personentage (PT) zu beauftragen. Vorbehaltlich von möglichen Änderungen der Gesetzeslage rund um den europäischen und den nationalen Emissionshandel erwartet der Auftraggeber, dass mindestens 50% der hier genannten Obergrenze für Personentage beauftragt werden wird. Sollte der Vertrag um jeweils ein Jahr verlängert werden, erwartet der Auftraggeber Aufgaben in der Höhe von 764 PT je Verlängerung (bis zu 25% des ursprünglichen Umfangs). Zum Zwecke einer ungefähren Kapazitätsplanung sehen wir in der Regel einen Bedarf von 500 PT pro Jahr, aber jeweils in 2028 und 2029 einen erhöhten Bedarf von etwa 1.000 PT. Die Auslastung über den Jahresverlauf kann sehr unterschiedlich ausfallen. Die Bereitstellung der Fachanwendungen muss in den allermeisten Fällen zu fixen gesetzlichen Fristen erfolgen. Dies hat zur Folge, dass mehrere Entwicklungsprojekte parallel bearbeitet werden müssen. Damit geht ein erhöhter Personalbedarf einher, der vom Auftragnehmer ab-gedeckt werden muss (z.B. zwei bis vier Entwicklungsressourcen arbeiten an einer Fach-anwendung, zeitgleich müssen bis zu vier Fachanwendungsprojekte bearbeitet werden). Die gesetzliche Fristsetzung kann vom Auftraggeber in der Regel leider nicht beeinflusst werden. Lot LOT-0003: Entwicklung und Wartung von Fachanwendungen für Vollzugsverfahren der DEHSt auf Basis des DEHSt-Software-Development Kits mit dem Schwerpunkt auf Migration von existierenden Fachanwendungen (Los 3). Los 3: Migration und Ablösung von Altsystemen . Nach dem aktuellen Planungsstand beabsichtigt der Auftraggeber in den ersten vier Jahren Aufgaben mit bis zu 4.472 (Personentage) PT zu beauftragen. Vorbehaltlich von möglichen Änderungen der Gesetzeslage rund um den europäischen und den nationalen Emissionshandel erwartet der Auftraggeber, dass mindestens 50% der hier genannten Obergrenze für Personentage beauftragt werden wird. Sollte der Vertrag um jeweils ein Jahr verlängert werden, erwartet der Auftraggeber Aufgaben in der Höhe von 1.118 PT je Verlängerung (bis zu 25% des ursprünglichen Umfangs).

result.text: PURPOSE NIOSH intends to support the Centers of Excellence in Total Worker Health® (TWH). These Centers will conduct rigorous research and translation activities to prevent harmful exposures, improve working conditions, and advance worker well-being. The Centers will develop practical, scalable solutions for employers and workers. All projects must use the NIOSH Worker Well-Being Questionnaire (WellBQ) and share data with the HERO Worker Well-Being Clearinghouse. Large Research Projects require economic evaluation. PRIORITY AREAS • High-risk occupations: First responders, vehicle mechanics, and technicians, with emphasis on occupational exposures, related health risks, and prevention strategies • Young workers, SMEs • Chronic disease • Mental health, stress • Substance use disorder • Artificial intelligence (AI), digital technologies This is a multi-component NOFO. COMPONENT STRUCTURE Percentages indicate maximum share of total budget. Overall Component (Required) Provides Center leadership and integration. Applicants should show strong coordination, scientific direction, and alignment across projects. Administration, Evaluation, and Emerging Issues Core (Required; up to 15%) Supports management and Center-wide evaluation. Applicants should describe oversight, data governance, and quality assurance.Optional activities include emerging issues and shared research resources. Outreach, Dissemination, and Impact Core (Required; up to 15%) Supports communication, worker/employer engagement, training, translation, implementation, and dissemination strategies. Research Projects (Required; about 60 to 70%) Includes all research activities. Applicants may propose a mix of projects. Research project distinctions are based on scope and complexity rather than cost. Projects should demonstrate scientific rigor and potential for sustained impact. Small Research Projects (Required; at least one project; up to 3 years) Exploratory, feasibility, early-stage intervention, surveillance, or measurement studies. Priority areas: high-risk occupations, young workers, SMEs. Should show innovation and potential to expand. Large Research Projects (Required; at least one project; up to 5 years) Multiyear etiologic, mechanistic, intervention, or translational studies. Priority areas: chronic disease, mental health, substance use disorder. Economic evaluation is required. Projects should include strong design and analytic plans. Pilot/Feasibility Program (Optional; 12–18 months) Short-term studies generating preliminary data or testing AI/digital technology approaches.

result.text: Crown Commercial Service (CCS) set up a dynamic purchasing system for a period of 60 months and has invited bidders to request to participate for the Cyber Security Services 3 DPS. result.text: Shropshire Council is undertaking Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) to understand the current market for digital solutions that support unpaid carers. This engagement will help inform the Council’s future commissioning approach before any decision is made about whether to tender, use an existing compliant route, develop an alternative model, or take no further procurement action. Shropshire Council has an established Unpaid Carer Support offer. Recently this has become an all-age offer supporting Young Carers and Parent Carers. The Unpaid Carers portal will be an online offer which will be available to Unpaid Carers 24/7 throughout the journey of their caring role. We are aware there are a large proportion of people who do not identify as an Unpaid Carer, we envisage the portal will support with that identification and will provide relevant up to date information to support families in a preventative manner. Any proposed solution should offer the following support: Increase the identification recognition and early interventions for unpaid Carers Delay and reduce the need to access high-cost statutory provision Improve accessibility to information, advice and guidance, improve links and signposting to services that are already available nationally, regionally and locally. Support Unpaid Carers to access self-help and self-management support to reduce the need for Unpaid Carers crisis interventions. Include access to Unpaid Carers 'self-assessment' focused on individualised outcomes The solution should have the capacity to collect and produce relative data regarding demographics, ethnicity, age range as well as information such as when and where the portal is accessed. Lot 1: . None

result.text: The DOE Office of Science (SC), Office of Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation (CMEI), Office of Environmental Management (EM), Office of Nuclear Energy (NE), Office of Electricity (OE), and Hydrocarbons and Geothermal Office (HGEO) hereby announce interest in receiving applications from interdisciplinary teams addressing the Genesis Mission National Science and Technology Challenges to accelerate scientific discovery and research and development (R&D) workflows using novel artificial intelligence (AI) models and frameworks. By achieving AI advantage, these teams will advance the DOE's mission and ensure America’s security and prosperity by addressing energy, environmental, and nuclear challenges through science and technology. Teams are encouraged to leverage the extensive scientific and data resources of the DOE/National Nuclear Security Administration (NNSA), the National Laboratories, U.S. industry, and academia. The resulting AI models and workflows, if successful, may be integrated into the American Science Cloud. DOE is soliciting new FY26 Phase I small team and Phase II large team applications in the following topic areas: advanced manufacturing, biotechnology, critical materials, nuclear fission, nuclear fusion, quantum information science, semiconductors and microelectronics, discovery science, and energy (see specific focus areas in Section III Program Descriptions). In addition, this RFA will remain available to allow the recipients of FY26 Phase I awards to apply for larger team Phase II awards. In a few weeks, DOE plans to amend the RFA to clarify the LOI and application guidelines for FY26 Phase II awards. In FY27, DOE plans to amend the RFA or to issue an alternative funding opportunity to update the topic and focus areas to allow a second competition of Phase I small team applications and Phase II large team applications.

parts.source: Myndigheten för kulturanalys inbjuder härmed leverantörer att ansöka om att få lämna anbud på rubricerad upphandling i enlighet med detta dokument och bifogade dokument. Underlaget avser att ge information om förutsättningarna för upphandlingen och uppdraget. Upphandlingen genomförs som förhandlat förfarande. Detta är steg 1, ansökansinbjudan. Leverantörer ges genom denna inbjudan möjlighet att ansöka om att få lämna anbud i steg 2. Upphandlingen avser ett webbaserat enkätverktyg som ska användas av Kulturanalys för datainsamling inom vissa av våra statistikområden, av 20 regioner för årlig uppföljning av kulturverksamheter med regionala bidrag och av Kulturrådet för årlig uppföljning av statliga bidrag inom kultursamverkansmodellen.

result.text: The subject of the tender is - per lot - the conclusion of a framework agreement for the benefit of the contracting authority as well as further beneficiaries and entitled accession parties. The future contractor(s) will act as an implementation partner and operator for the contracting authority (ITSCare) and its shareholders (currently AOK Baden-Württemberg, AOK Hessen, AOK Rheinland-Pfalz/Saarland) as well as potentially entitled accession parties to provide and operate fully multi-client capable - central IT infrastructure on-premises as well as in private and public cloud delivery models (Lot 1) and - decentralised services (Lot 2). This includes in particular the following services: - Assumption of the services from the current external service provider and operation of the services regarding Lot 1 initially with a high on-premises share by the contractor. A transformation of the services into alternative delivery and service models must be possible. - For Lot 2, the tendered services are taken over from the existing external provider, modernised as part of the transition and operated permanently by the contractor. - The operation is carried out largely under the full responsibility of the contractor. Entitled accession parties in the aforementioned sense are - other IT service providers in the AOK system whose shareholders are exclusively AOKs or their joint subsidiaries held exclusively by AOKs, - joint subsidiaries of all AOKs and - AOKs that are not the shareholders of ITSCare, and which are each to be given the opportunity to accede to the contracts (framework agreements) in order to be able to participate in the services agreed in the framework agreement. The services shall be provided during a standard term of 4 years with a twice renewable option of 2 years each. Before the start of the standard term, there is a 12-month transition phase during which the services are transferred from the previous provider to the contractor. Following the standard term (extended if applicable by exercising the aforementioned options), a transition-out phase takes place, the duration of which is a maximum of 12 months. Accessions are possible until the expiry of the non-extended standard term of 4 years of the respective contract. result.text: The Stadtwerke Ingolstadt Beteiligungen GmbH (SWI) is planning the transformation of the existing SAP R/3 landscape to SAP S/4HANA using the brownfield approach. The subject of the tender is the award of services in several lots. Providers can apply for individual lots or for several lots. Licence and hardware requirements (HANA sizing, DB, infrastructure) must be taken into account by the bidder. Sustainability aspects (energy-efficient data centres, minimisation of dual operation) must be presented. Management of the SAP S/4HANA migration project (brownfield approach) programme in the context of this tender. The contractor shall provide project management, taking into account the assurance of governance, planning and reporting obligations (see service description); introduction of New GL incl. ledger solution, document splitting, profit centre balance sheet and FI AA; technical conception of FI/CO as well as customising in terms of the target ledger structure; subject. Migration of debtors/creditors to the business partner model; harmonisation & cleansing as a prerequisite for S/4; subject. Creation of technical concepts for affected modules and cross-sectional topics; target architecture for migration & integration; subject. Harmonisation & implementation of workflows (incoming invoice, PR/order) and catalogue connection; use of SAP standard; integration of archive/output; subject. GDPR-compliant archiving and deletion concept; SAP ILM as reference, equivalent solutions permitted (fully SAP-integrated, audit-proof, GDPR-compliant).

parts.source: Die Stadtwerke Ingolstadt Beteiligungen GmbH (SWI) plant die Transformation der bestehenden SAP R/3-Landschaft auf SAP S/4HANA im Brownfield-Ansatz. Gegenstand der Ausschreibung ist die Vergabe von Leistungen in mehreren Losen. Anbieter können sich auf einzelne Lose oder auf mehrere Lose bewerben. Lizenz- und Hardware-Anforderungen (HANA Sizing, DB, Infrastruktur) sind vom Bieter zu berücksichtigen. Nachhaltigkeitsaspekte (energieeffiziente Rechenzentren, Minimierung Doppelbetrieb) sind darzustellen. Steuerung des SAP S/4HANA Migrationsprojekt (Brownfield-Ansatz) Programms im Kontext dieser Ausschreibung. Der Auftragnehmer erbringt die Projektleitung unter Berücksichtigung der Sicherstellung von Governance, Planungs- und Berichtspflichten (s. Leistungsbeschreibung); Einführung New GL inkl. Ledergerlösung, Belegsplitt, Profit Center Bilanz und FI AA; fachliche Konzeption FI/CO sowie Customizing im Sinne der Ziel Ledgerstruktur.; Gegenstand. Migration von Debitoren/Kreditoren in das Geschäftspartner Modell; Harmonisierung & Bereinigung als Voraussetzung für S/4.; Gegenstand. Erstellung fachlicher Konzepte für betroffene Module und Querschnittsthemen; Zielarchitektur für Migration & Integration.; Gegenstand. Harmonisierung & Implementierung von Workflows (Eingangsrechnung, BANF/Bestellung) und Katalog Anbindung; Nutzung SAP Standard; Integration Archiv/Output.; Gegenstand. DSGVO konformes Archivierungs und Löschkonzept; SAP ILM als Referenz, gleichwertige Lösungen zulässig (voll SAP integriert, prüfungssicher, DSGVO konform).

result.text: The subject matter of the tendered service is the technical monitoring and support of the contracting authority in the area of expansion and maintenance of applications for test automation as well as in the creation of quality assurance components (QA). Further information on the specific subject matter of the contract can be found in the service description attached to the procurement documents (Annex 1). Bundesdruckerei has its own teams in the area of system testing for sovereign and non-sovereign documents, which are responsible for quality assurance during the regular introduction of extensions and changes to the "German System". The activities in this area include carrying out various tests on the individual subsystems and the overall system. These tests are based on an in-house test strategy and ensure compliance with all new and existing functional and non-functional requirements. These include regression, load and performance tests, among others. Different applications for test automation are used to carry out the tests. For the continuous expansion and maintenance of test automation and for the further creation of QA components, Bundesdruckerei is looking for a partner to accompany Bundesdruckerei's activities in this area and provide selective support for the existing teams both internally and externally. Further information on the specific subject matter of the contract can be found in the service description attached to the procurement documents (Annex 1)

parts.source: Gegenstand der ausgeschriebenen Leistung ist die technische Begleitung und Unterstützung des Auftraggebers im Bereich Ausbau und Pflege von Applikationen für die Testautomatisierung sowie bei der Erstellung von Qualitätssicherungskomponenten (QA). Nähere Informationen zum konkreten Leistungsgegenstand können der den Vergabeunterlagen beigefügten Leistungsbeschreibung (Anlage 1) entnommen werden Die Bundesdruckerei verfügt im Bereich des Systemtests für hoheitliche und nichthoheitliche Dokumente über eigene Teams, die in Verantwortung für die Qualitätssicherung der regelmäßigen Einführungen von Erweiterungen und Änderungen am "Deutschen System" zuständig sind. Die Tätigkeiten in diesem Bereich umfassen die Durchführung verschiedener Tests auf den einzelnen Subsystemen und dem Gesamtsystem. Diese Tests orientieren sich an einer hausinternen Teststrategie und sichern die Erfüllung aller neuen und der bestehenden funktionalen und nichtfunktionalen Anforderungen. Dazu gehören unter anderem Regressions-, Last- und Performancetests. Für die Durchführung der Tests werden unterschiedliche Applikationen für die Testautomatisierung eingesetzt. Zum stetigen Ausbau und der Pflege der Testautomatisierung und zur weiteren Erstellung von QA-Komponenten sucht die Bundesdruckerei einen Partner, der die Tätigkeiten der Bundesdruckerei in diesem Bereich begleitet und intern wie extern punktuell Unterstützung für die vorhandenen Teams leistet. result.text: Queen’s University Belfast requires a Research Intelligence Tool to support institutional research and innovation strategy, planning, and evaluation. The tool will enable benchmarking of research performance, identification of emerging research strengths, monitoring of collaboration and partnership activity, and support planning for research assessment exercises and strategic planning across Faculties and Schools. Queen’s will develop requirements based on institutional needs, including functional fit, data quality, usability, interoperability, alignment with research culture and responsible metrics principles, and value for money. Key users will include academic staff, Faculty Deans of Research, Research Strategy & Policy Team, Research Development, Global Research Partnerships, Business Alliance, Library (Open Research), Global Marketing and Reputation, and the Research Intelligence Team.

result.text: Supply of thermal orthophotos for the area of Region Hannover 1. Background The Region Hannover has set itself the ambitious goal of being climate-neutral by the year 2035. The energy-efficient refurbishment of the building stock is a central component for achieving this goal. In particular, improving the thermal insulation of buildings offers considerable potential for reducing CO2 emissions and increasing energy efficiency. In order to raise awareness among owners of residential and non-residential buildings regarding potential heat losses and refurbishment needs, a comprehensive thermal imaging map is to be created. The aim is to create a low-threshold information basis through a visually prepared presentation of thermal radiation data. The interactive online map should make it possible to classify one's own building stock in a regional context and initiate further steps if necessary. By linking with the advisory services of the climate protection agency Region Hannover (KSA) as well as existing funding programmes, the project is intended to trigger concrete refurbishment measures. 2. Contents and procedure The subject of the contract is the supply of thermographic digital orthophotos (DOP), i.e., distortion-free and georeferenced thermography recordings, for the area of Region Hannover. The contractor's delivery service includes carrying out the flight including preparation as well as the transmission of the processed data.

parts.source: Lieferung von Thermalorthofotos für das Gebiet der Region Hannover 1. Hintergrund Die Region Hannover hat sich das ehrgeizige Ziel gesetzt, bis zum Jahr 2035 klimaneutral zu sein. Die energetische Sanierung des Gebäudebestandes ist ein zentraler Baustein zur Erreichung dieses Zieles. Besonders die Verbesserung der Wärmedämmung von Gebäuden bietet erhebliches Potential zur Reduzierung von CO2-Emissionen und zur Steigerung der Energieeffizienz. Um Eigentümerinnen und Eigentümer von Wohn- und Nichtwohngebäuden für mögliche Wärmeverluste und Sanierungsbedarfe zu sensibilisieren, soll eine flächendeckende Wärmebildkarte erstellt werden. Ziel ist es, durch eine visuell aufbereitete Darstellung von Wärmestrahlungsdaten eine niedrigschwellige Informationsgrundlage zu schaffen. Die interaktive Online-Karte soll es ermöglichen, den eigenen Gebäudebestand im regionalen Kontext einzuordnen und bei Bedarf weitere Schritte einzuleiten. Durch die Verknüpfung mit den Beratungsangeboten der Klimaschutzagentur Region Hannover (KSA) sowie bestehenden Förderprogrammen soll das Projekt konkrete Sanierungsmaßnahmen anstoßen. 2. Inhalte und Ablauf Gegenstand des Auftrags ist die Lieferung von thermografischen digitalen Orthophotos (DOP), also verzerrungsfreien und georeferenzierten Thermografieaufnahmen, für das Gebiet der Region Hannover. Die Lieferleistung des Auftragnehmers beinhaltet die Durchführung der Befliegung inkl. Vorbereitung sowie die Übermittlung der aufbereiteten Daten.

result.text: Background Innovate UK Business Connect brings together businesses, researchers, investors and partners to accelerate innovation across the UK. As part of UK Research and Innovation (UKRI), and a strategic delivery partner to Innovate UK, we connect organisations to funding opportunities, partnerships and expertise to help ideas move from concept to scale. One of the key tools for making these connections is events. We deliver a diverse portfolio of in-person, virtual and hybrid events, ranging from webinars and workshops to large-scale conferences and exhibitions. To support the effective planning, delivery and evaluation of these events, we are seeking proposals from suppliers who can provide a modern event management system that streamlines event operations, enhances the participant experience and supports data-driven decision-making. Description of work Innovate UK Business Connect is seeking tenders from providers who can supply a single event management system that supports the end-to-end event lifecycle, including event creation, registration management, attendee communications, speaker and exhibitor management, networking, reporting and post-event evaluation. The system should integrate with existing business systems where required and provide a single source of truth for event delivery teams. This aligns with the organisation's wider objective of ensuring events are outcome-led, measurable and supported by efficient registration, communication and reporting processes. The event management system should: • Deliver an intuitive and user-friendly delegate journey from registration through to post-event follow-up • Improve the event experience for speakers and exhibitors • Reduce manual administration and improve operational efficiency • Provide real-time visibility of registrations, attendance, engagement and event performance • Support both virtual and in-person event delivery models • Enable consistent data capture and reporting to demonstrate event impact and ROI • Support accessibility, compliance and data protection requirements The platform must support multiple user roles and permission levels to reflect different operational needs across the organisation. As a minimum, the system should accommodate the following user groups: • Event Managers o Full end-to-end event management capabilities o Creation, configuration and administration of events o Management of registrations, attendee communications, speakers and exhibitors o Access to event-level reporting, analytics and post-event evaluation data • Marketing Managers o Access to update and manage event webpages and associated content o Access to registration, engagement and performance reporting • Integrated Systems o Administration of integrations between the event management platform and our CRM system (Workbooks) o Management of data flows, field mapping, data quality and synchronisation processes o Access to reporting, data exports and system configuration relating to integrations • System Administrators o A small number of designated super users (typically two to three individuals) o Full platform administration rights, including user management, permissions, integrations, security settings and system configuration We deliver a large and diverse portfolio of business-to-business events. Historically, this has included more than 300 events per year and generating approximately 60,000 delegate registrations annually. The event management platform must be capable of supporting a range of event formats, scales and audience sizes, including: • In person events: We deliver approximately 100 in-person events each year, typically attracting between 30 and 2,000 delegates to each. Most events are free to attend and may span one or more days. We do not require onsite event delivery support from the appointment supplier; however the platform must provide the functionality and tools to enable our team to manage attendee registration and onsite event operations, and provide a seamless and efficient onsite experience for attendees • Online Events: We deliver close to 200 fully online events annually. The majority are webinars, including webinar series and interactive workshops. We also run a small number of larger-scale virtual conferences and exhibitions, some of which take place over multiple days. The platform should provide a seamless user experience for both organisers and attendees and support the delivery of events of varying size and complexity. • Hybrid: A smaller proportion of our events are hybrid, combining in-person and virtual attendance. The platform should support hybrid event delivery and provide a consistent registration, communication and reporting experience across both audience groups. The proposed solution must be capable of supporting this volume of activity while providing robust registration management, attendee communications, data integration, reporting and analytics across all event formats. Timings This is a two-stage evaluation process. We will do an initially score of each supplier bid with the top two or three scoring suppliers invited to provide a demonstration. This will be the opportunity for the selected suppliers to demonstrate the setup of an event using a given scenario. Anticipated timeline: • October: demo • November: final evaluation • November - December: Contract is awarded • 1 April 2027: Contract starts • April - September: Onboarding, training, templates created and integrations built • September onwards: Events start to be managed from the platform Cost The maximum value of this requirement over the three-year period is a maximum of £600,000.00 excluding VAT. This contract is structured as an initial two-year period with a maximum budget of £400,000.00 excluding VAT with an optional 12-month extension valued at maximum £200,000.00 excluding VAT. Submission In response to this tender, please provide the information listed below.

The event management system should: • Deliver an intuitive and user-friendly delegate journey from registration through to post-event follow-up • Improve the event experience for speakers and exhibitors • Reduce manual administration and improve operational efficiency • Provide real-time visibility of registrations, attendance, engagement and event performance • Support both virtual and in-person event delivery models • Enable consistent data capture and reporting to demonstrate event impact and ROI • Support accessibility, compliance and data protection requirements The platform must support multiple user roles and permission levels to reflect different operational needs across the organisation. As a minimum, the system should accommodate the following user groups: • Event Managers o Full end-to-end event management capabilities o Creation, configuration and administration of events o Management of registrations, attendee communications, speakers and exhibitors o Access to event-level reporting, analytics and post-event evaluation data • Marketing Managers o Access to update and manage event webpages and associated content o Access to registration, engagement and performance reporting • Integrated Systems o Administration of integrations between the event management platform and our CRM system (Workbooks) o Management of data flows, field mapping, data quality and synchronisation processes o Access to reporting, data exports and system configuration relating to integrations • System Administrators o A small number of designated super users (typically two to three individuals) o Full platform administration rights, including user management, permissions, integrations, security settings and system configuration We deliver a large and diverse portfolio of business-to-business events. Historically, this has included more than 300 events per year and generating approximately 60,000 delegate registrations annually. The event management platform must be capable of supporting a range of event formats, scales and audience sizes, including: • In person events: We deliver approximately 100 in-person events each year, typically attracting between 30 and 2,000 delegates to each. Most events are free to attend and may span one or more days. We do not require onsite event delivery support from the appointment supplier; however the platform must provide the functionality and tools to enable our team to manage attendee registration and onsite event operations, and provide a seamless and efficient onsite experience for attendees • Online Events: We deliver close to 200 fully online events annually. The majority are webinars, including webinar series and interactive workshops. We also run a small number of larger-scale virtual conferences and exhibitions, some of which take place over multiple days. The platform should provide a seamless user experience for both organisers and attendees and support the delivery of events of varying size and complexity. • Hybrid: A smaller proportion of our events are hybrid, combining in-person and virtual attendance. The platform should support hybrid event delivery and provide a consistent registration, communication and reporting experience across both audience groups. The proposed solution must be capable of supporting this volume of activity while providing robust registration management, attendee communications, data integration, reporting and analytics across all event formats. Timings This is a two-stage evaluation process. We will do an initially score of each supplier bid with the top two or three scoring suppliers invited to provide a demonstration. This will be the opportunity for the selected suppliers to demonstrate the setup of an event using a given scenario. Anticipated timeline: • October: demo • November: final evaluation • November - December: Contract is awarded • 1 April 2027: Contract starts • April - September: Onboarding, training, templates created and integrations built • September onwards: Events start to be managed from the platform Cost The maximum value of this requirement over the three-year period is a maximum of £600,000.00 excluding VAT. This contract is structured as an initial two-year period with a maximum budget of £400,000.00 excluding VAT with an optional 12-month extension valued at maximum £200,000.00 excluding VAT. result.text: The Board of Trustees for the National Galleries of Scotland ("NGS") wish to award a Contract for the Provision of Audience Research Services. The Service Provider is required to conduct Audience Research to provide insight and analysis about our visitors in order to support the Organisation’s 2030 Strategy, Business Plan and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), special projects and inform organisation-wide strategic planning. The Service Provider shall be a member of, accredited by, or operate in accordance with the standards, codes of conduct and professional requirements of the Market Research Society (MRS) or an equivalent recognised professional body for market research, social research, insight or analytics. This Contract shall primarily provide Fieldwork Surveys and associated Project Management, Client Data Access, Analysis and Reporting for each of our four gallery sites. Services will be agreed to on an “as required” basis with no commitment to a minimum volume of work. NGS may, at its absolute discretion, require the Service Provider to provide Audience Research Services at this fifth site, currently under construction, at any time during the Contract term. If permitted by applicable procurement legislation, where additional audience research requirements arise during the Contract term that constitute an extension of the Services, NGS reserves the right to procure such additional services from the Service Provider. For full details of the Contract Requirements please refer to the associated Tender and Contract Documents. The Service Provider must have a clear understanding of the contract requirements and the organisational needs of NGS. As part of the tender exercise, the Service Provider must detail a robust and flexible methodology for conducting Audience Research Services that will meet all data capture requirements. There is no commitment to a minimum spend over the duration of the Contract. Under this Contract, no minimum spend is guaranteed. The agreement will be non-exclusive i.e. NGS reserves the right, in certain, circumstances, to procure out with the Contract Agreement, as and when required. In the event of unsatisfactory performance by the successful Service Provider and the termination of the contract by either party, NGS reserves the right to negotiate the continuance of the services with the second and third placed Service Providers. Lot 1: . The procurement will be conducted through the use of the Open Procedure. Service Providers must complete and submit both an SPD and Tender response. Economic Operators may be excluded from this competition if they are in any of the situations referred to in Regulation 58 of the Public Contracts (Scotland) Regulations 2015. Given the nature of the contract, Tenderers must comply with minimum security requirements. The Service Provider must obtain valid Cyber Essentials Basic (or equivalent) certification prior to the Contract Commencement Date and maintain throughout the Contract term including any extension periods. It is desirable that the Service Provider hold current ISO/IEC 27001 (or equivalent) certification or otherwise Tenderers must demonstrate equivalent information security management arrangements as part of the quality assessment. Full details are set out in the Tender and Contract Documents. The maximum available budget to deliver the Core Contract Requirements is 60,000 GBP per annum excluding VAT. Tenderers are required to submit pricing that can be delivered within this annual budget for Years 1 – 5 of the Contract, including any optional extension periods. Any Tender exceeding the maximum available budget, may be deemed unaffordable and may be excluded from further consideration. Tenderers must provide fixed prices for Years 1 – 3 of the Contract, and indicative prices for Years 4 & 5. The prices submitted for Years 4 and 5 shall represent the maximum prices payable during any extension period unless NGS approves a formal change request due to the Service Provider sufficiently demonstrating exceptional circumstances. Cost Control Mechanisms for Years 4 & 5 are detailed under Schedule 2 of the Contract Agreement. For this Tender Competition, and for commercial evaluation purposes, NGS reserves the right to assess affordability against a maximum annual budget of 60,000 GBP for each contract year, including any optional extension periods. NGS reserves the right not to award where it considers submitted pricing to exceed available funding. Information in respect of Optional Contract Requirements, and estimate additional spend, has been provided at section V1.3 ‘Additional ‘Information’. The ‘Estimate Total Contract Value’ provided at II.1.5, includes both estimate spend for Core Contract Requirements and estimate spend for Optional Contract Requirements.. The top three highest scoring Tenderers (price & quality combined score) will be invited to a Tender Presentation stage on 4th and/or 5th November 2026 (dates may be subject to change). Full details provided in the Tender Documents.

result.text: SKI hereby invites tenders for a dynamic purchasing system regarding the procurement of IT consultancy services within 14 service areas with associated sub-areas, sub-categories and services. Below are the 14 service areas with associated sub-areas indicated. The actual services that can be procured in the 14 service areas are described in detail in Appendix C. Subject of the system: Service area 1: IT-related strategies Sub-area: Preparation of IT-related strategies Sub-area: Implementation of IT-related strategies Sub-area: Evaluation and updating as well as impact assessment of strategies Service area 2: Business needs, business case and benefit realisation Sub-area: Identification of business needs and preparation of business cases Sub-area: Realisation of business cases Sub-area: Follow-up on business cases Service area 3: IT tendering Sub-area: Preparation of tenders Sub-area: Execution of tenders Service area 4: IT security, business continuity and IT compliance Sub-area: Establishment of IT security Sub-area: Crisis management, business continuity and disaster recovery Sub-area: IT compliance Service area 5: IT architecture Sub-area: Establishment of an IT architecture Sub-area: Review and adjustment of existing IT architecture Service area 6: IT governance Sub-area: Establishment of IT governance Sub-area: Organisation of system management Sub-area: Establishment of IT supplier management Service area 7: Project and programme management Sub-area: Project management – the traditional waterfall model Sub-area: Management of agile projects Sub-area: Programme management Service area 8: Data processing Sub-area: Data analysis and reporting Sub-area: Use of external data Sub-area: Conversion, cleaning and archiving of data Service area 9: Advice on software licences Sub-area: Open source software vs. closed source software Sub-area: Determination of the size of specific licences, as well as the conditions associated with the use Service area 10: Infrastructure and hardware Sub-area: Setup, configuration and operation of networks Sub-area: Setup, configuration and operation of servers Sub-area: Setup, configuration and operation of clients Service area 11: Test Sub-area: IT testing of development according to the traditional waterfall model Sub-area: Agile IT testing Service area 12: Development of new functionality Sub-area: IT development according to the traditional waterfall model Sub-area: Agile IT development Service area 13: Adaptation of existing IT systems Sub-area: IT development with a view to adapting existing IT systems Service area 14: IT system operation Sub-area: Operation of IT systems The system is divided into 2 categories: • Category 1 Competence purchase • Category 2 Task purchase The same services can be procured in both categories, but the categories differ in that the customer in category 1 must procure one or more specific competence(s), while the customer in category 2 must have a specific task solved. The customer's objective purchasing need thus dictates which category is to be used. • In category 1 the customer specifies their need for competencies within IT consultancy services and need for number of hours, after which the Tenderer offers competencies and prices. • In category 2 the customer defines the task, after which the tenderer offers a task solution in accordance with the customer's statement of requirements. It is voluntary for all SKI's customers, as stated in Appendix B, Customer List, to make use of the system when they need to procure IT consultancy services. Procurement of Competence purchase In category 1 customers can procure IT consultancy services within the 14 service areas described in Appendix C, to fulfil the customer's competence needs. The consultancy services can be procured in 2 ways. 1. Remuneration form 1: Purchase of consultancy hours (number of hours x hourly rate). 2. Remuneration form 2: Purchase of ongoing services (monthly remuneration x number of months + estimated number of hours (time spent) x hourly rate).; Procurement of IT consultancy services for task solution In category 2 the customers can procure IT consultancy services within the 14 service areas described in Appendix C, to fulfil a specific task. The consultancy services can be procured in 3 ways. 1. Remuneration form 1: Purchase of IT consultancy services for the solution of the described task (number x hourly rate). 2. Remuneration form 2: Purchase of ongoing services (monthly remuneration x number of months + estimated number of hours (time spent) x hourly rate). 3. Remuneration form 3: Purchase of task solution at a fixed price.

Det er frivilligt for alle SKI’s kunder, som fremgår af bilag B, Kundeliste, at gøre brug af systemet, når de skal anskaffe it-konsulentydelser. Konsulentydelserne kan anskaffes på 3 måder. 1. Vederlagsform 1: Køb af it-konsulentydelser til løsning af beskrevne opgave (antal x time-pris). 2. Vederlagsform 2: Køb af løbende ydelser (månedligt vederlag x antal måneder + estimeret antal timer (medgået tid) x timepris). 3. Vederlagsform 3: Køb af opgaveløsning til fast pris.

The procurement is intended to support Fairhive's requirement for an LMS platform that enables effective learning management, compliance training, reporting, user administration and integration with Fairhive's wider systems environment. The RFQ states that Fairhive wishes to appoint a single supplier to provide, implement, configure, support and maintain the LMS in accordance with the specification. The requirement is expected to include: 1. Supply of a hosted Learning Management System platform. 2. Configuration of workflows, roles, permissions, learning pathways, dashboards, notifications and branding. 3. Implementation support, including mobilisation, discovery, implementation planning, testing, user acceptance testing, go-live support and hypercare. 4. Data migration support, including extraction support, mapping, cleansing support, migration, reconciliation and validation. 5. Microsoft Entra ID Single Sign-On and user provisioning integration. 6. Microsoft 365 integrations, including Microsoft Teams and Outlook calendar integration. 7. Administrator, manager and end-user training, including materials and train-the-trainer or digital resources. 8. Initial content and SCORM set-up, including upload, configuration and validation of SCORM 1.2/2004 and other agreed content. 9. Ongoing hosting, storage, backups, disaster recovery, support, service levels, maintenance, updates, escalation and account management. 10. Reporting, dashboards and scheduled reporting. Suppliers will be expected to demonstrate: 1. Relevant experience implementing and supporting Learning Management Systems for a housing association, public sector organisation or similarly regulated environment. 2. A functional solution that supports learning pathways, compliance training management, reporting and dashboards, certification, SCORM compliance, accessibility, mobile functionality, workflow automation, manager functionality, learner experience and Microsoft 365 integration. 3. A clear implementation, data migration and training methodology, including project mobilisation, configuration, testing, user acceptance testing, data migration, training, go-live support and hypercare. 4. Robust information security, compliance and business continuity arrangements, including ISO27001, Cyber Essentials Plus, UK GDPR compliance, data hosting, resilience, disaster recovery, business continuity and incident management. 5. Effective support, service desk, account management, service level, escalation, reporting, quarterly review, product roadmap and continuous improvement arrangements. 6. Measurable social value and sustainability commitments, including community investment, skills and employment support, carbon reduction, digital inclusion, volunteering, equality, diversity and inclusion, supplier diversity and wider environmental sustainability initiatives. Fairhive intends to use the procurement documentation and evaluation process to assess the optimum combination of quality, social value and price. The RFQ defines Most Advantageous Tender as the tender offering the optimum combination of quality, social value and price in accordance with the evaluation methodology. Particular emphasis is expected to be placed on: 1. Functional LMS capability and user experience. 2. Compliance training management and reporting. 3. Data security, UK GDPR compliance and hosting arrangements. 4. Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Entra ID integration. 5. Implementation, data migration and training support. 6. Service desk, support, service levels and account management. 7. Social value, sustainability and measurable community benefits. Lot 1: .

result.text: The contracting authority for the services tendered here is the University Hospital of Cologne (AöR), one of the largest tertiary care centres in North Rhine-Westphalia with over 1.500 planned beds, around 60.000 inpatient cases and more than 350.000 outpatient cases annually. The contracting authority intends to commission an experienced management consultant specialising in the healthcare sector to support the hospital in overcoming its financial, organisational and structural challenges and to develop and implement a comprehensive transformation programme together with the commercial management. The aim of the services to be awarded is to sustainably improve the economic performance of the University Hospital of Cologne by identifying, prioritising and implementing revenue-increasing and cost-reducing measures, as well as adapting organisational structures and processes to future requirements. The programme is intended to achieve short-term liquidity and earnings contributions, while at the same time strengthening the hospital's strategic competitiveness in the medium and long term. As part of the contract performance, the contractor will record the existing potential, derive a robust portfolio of measures for all relevant service areas, manage the implementation of these measures in a structured programme and monitor them using key figure-based controlling. Furthermore, it is expected that the contractor will install an effective change management system that involves employees, the faculty and other stakeholders in the transformation process. The identified operational potential lies primarily in the medical service portfolio (optimisation of case mix, length of stay, operating theatre capacities and outpatient care), in material and non-personnel cost management, in the structures of subsidiaries and administrative areas, and in personnel requirements and shift planning. The contractor's services are expected to include in particular the following areas: - Analysis of the economic starting position, including benchmarking with comparable hospitals, uncovering earnings and efficiency potential, and deriving a robust business case. - Development, prioritisation and detailing of a catalogue of measures for revenue growth (e.g. operating theatre utilisation, expansion of highly specialised services) and for cost reduction (e.g. materials management, energy costs, process digitalisation, personnel structure). - Establishment and operation of a central Project Management Office (PMO) to manage all sub-projects, including change management, communication strategy and management training. - Conception and implementation of a key figure-based management and reporting system ("Performance Dashboard") as well as sustainable implementation controlling to ensure the permanent anchoring of the improvements achieved. In addition, the contractor must identify further potential for increasing economic performance, develop corresponding solution proposals and support their implementation. We are looking for a "driving force" that proactively contributes.

parts.source: Der Auftraggeber der hier ausgeschriebenen Leistungen ist das Universitätsklinikum Köln (AöR), eines der größten Häuser der Maximalversorgung in Nordrhein-Westfalen mit über 1.500 Planbetten, rund 60.000 stationären sowie mehr als 350.000 ambulanten Fällen jährlich. Der Auftraggeber beabsichtigt, einen erfahrenen, auf das Gesundheitswesen spezialisierten Unternehmensberater zu beauftragen, der das Klinikum in der Bewältigung seiner finanziellen, organisatorischen und strukturellen Herausforderungen unterstützt und gemeinsam mit der kaufmännischen Direktion ein umfassendes Transformationsprogramm entwickelt und umsetzt. Ziel der zu vergebenden Leistungen ist es, die wirtschaftliche Leistungsfähigkeit des Universitätsklinikums Köln nachhaltig zu verbessern, indem erlössteigernde und kostenreduzierende Maßnahmen identifiziert, priorisiert und implementiert sowie organisatorische Strukturen und Prozesse an die zukünftigen Anforderungen angepasst werden. Das Programm soll kurzfristige Liquiditäts- und Ergebnisbeiträge erzielen, zugleich aber mittel- und langfristig die strategische Wettbewerbsfähigkeit des Hauses stärken. Im Rahmen der Auftragserbringung wird der Auftragnehmer die vorhandenen Potenziale erfassen, daraus ein belastbares Maßnahmenportfolio für alle relevanten Leistungsbereiche ableiten, die Umsetzung dieser Maßnahmen in einem strukturierten Programm steuern und durch ein kennzahlenbasiertes Controlling überwachen. Darüber hinaus wird erwartet, dass der Auftragnehmer ein wirksames Change-Management installiert, das Mitarbeitende, Fakultät und weitere Stakeholder in den Transformationsprozess einbindet. Die identifizierten operativen Potenziale liegen vor allem im medizinischen Leistungsportfolio (Optimierung von Fallmix, Verweildauer, OP-Kapazitäten und Ambulantisierung), in der Material- und Sachkostenbewirtschaftung, in den Strukturen der Tochtergesellschaften und administrativen Bereichen sowie in der Personalbedarfs- und Schichtplanung. Die Leistungen des Auftragnehmers umfassen voraussichtlich insbesondere die folgenden Bereiche: - Analyse der wirtschaftlichen Ausgangslage, einschließlich Benchmarking mit Vergleichshäusern, Aufdeckung von Ergebnis- und Effizienzpotenzialen sowie Ableitung eines belastbaren Business-Case. - Entwicklung, Priorisierung und Detaillierung eines Maßnahmenkatalogs zur Erlössteigerung (z. B. OP-Auslastung, Ausbau hochspezialisierter Leistungen) sowie zur Kostenreduktion (z. B. Materialwirtschaft, Energiekosten, Prozessdigitalisierung, Personalstruktur). - Einrichtung und Betrieb eines zentralen Projektmanagement-Office (PMO) zur Steuerung aller Teilprojekte, einschließlich Change-Management, Kommunikationsstrategie und Schulung der Führungskräfte. - Konzeption und Implementierung eines kennzahlenbasierten Steuerungs- und Berichtssystems ("Performance Dashboard") sowie eines nachhaltigen Umsetzungscontrollings zur Sicherstellung der dauerhaften Verankerung der erzielten Verbesserungen. Darüber hinaus hat der Auftragnehmer weitere Potenziale zur Steigerung der wirtschaftlichen Leistungsfähigkeit zu identifizieren, entsprechende Lösungsvorschläge zu erarbeiten und die Umsetzung zu begleiten. Gesucht wird eine "treibende Kraft", die sich proaktiv einbringt.

result.text: Background Troms County (TFK) manages buildings of 218,000 m2, comprising i.a. schools, sports facilities, dental clinics, workplaces and other county buildings. The cleaning services are carried out by approx. 130 cleaners organised by teams, with a focus on flexible work forms, efficient use of resources and quality in the service delivery. The County municipality needs a more uniform, digital and documentable follow-up of cleaning across buildings, rooms and areas. The current systems do not provide sufficient support for registration and follow-up of work performed, deviations and quality measurements. Therefore there is a need for a system that makes it easy for cleaners to register work and register conditions that affect cleaning, for example rooms that cannot be cleaned, deviations or a lack of periodic cleaning. At the same time, the county needs a better overview and management information. Managers should be able to follow the status per building, area and room, identify areas that have not been cleaned and get a better basis for planning capacity, resource use and absence management. The cleaning quality shall be measured and documented in accordance with NS-INSTA 800. TFK would like systems that provide good support for quality follow-up, reporting and analysis, which contribute to increased user friendliness, better decision making and more efficient operation. The procurement is being made to establish a future orientated digital system that provides a better overview, more uniform practice, better documentation and more efficient management of deviations, quality follow-up and resource planning. Description of the assignment The assignment includes the delivery, establishment, operation and support of a digital cleaning system for Troms County. The system shall provide an overview of cleaning per building, room and area and it can be used by cleaners, substitutes, managers, administrators and operations managers where the work is carried out. The system shall support planning, implementation, documentation and follow-up of the cleaning services. The system shall, among other things: Give easy registration of completed cleaning, status and deviations. Support registration and follow-up of periodic cleaning. Give an overview of rooms and areas that have not been cleaned or where deviations are registered. Support quality measurements and documentation in accordance with NS-INSTA 800. Offer reports and management information that supports follow-up, documentation, analysis and resource planning. Support both short term and long term planning of assignments and resources. Be able to integrate with existing and future MOM systems, as well as facilitate future integrations with other support systems, including possibilities for future use of sensor technology, such as dispensers, waste handling, machines and robots. The delivery shall include the necessary establishment and configuration of the building and room structure, user roles and access management, as well as training, user support and administrative assistance in connection with the introduction and use of the system. TFK would like a user friendly and visually oriented system that facilitates efficient operation, good quality control and future development of the cleaning services. Further requirements for functionality, technical conditions, security, privacy, integrations and service level are stated in the requirement specification.

result.text: The objective of the procurement is to cover the OFA companies ́need for software and a system for secure printing and scanning for all users. The system shall contribute to standardising and making printing and scanning solutions more efficient in the OFA cooperation and supporting joint ICT strategy and security requirements. The software shall be easy to use for final users and easy to operate for key personnel, while facilitating resource and cost efficient operation. The system shall optimise the use of existing servers. There are requirements for cooperation between the software supplier, suppliers of multi-function machines (MFP) and the ICT departments in the OFA cooperation. The ICT operations are largely centralised, facilitating an efficient implementation and follow-up of the system. The procurement does not include physical hardware (MFP), but the software shall support existing and upcoming MFP deliveries through standardised interface and authentication systems. The system shall be flexible and adaptable to changes in the machinery, infrastructure and organisation of ICT services in the contract period. The aim is to establish a secure, user friendly, functional and cost efficient print system that requires minimal local administration and efficient interaction across the OFA companies.

result.text: The University of Edinburgh is undertaking preliminary market engagement to improve our understanding of current and emerging supplier capabilities, products and solutions for a Student Record Platform. The University is interested in student record systems that can integrate with its existing landscape, with the potential to rationalise and simplify the complexity of its current environment. This includes supporting areas such as exceptional circumstances, scholarships and assessment and progression,with the aim of delivering a more streamlined and effective solution. The University currently has contractual arrangements in place for its existing student record system. This engagement forms part of longer-term planning and is intended to improve understanding of how the market is evolving, inform the University's business requirements and support the development of its strategic planning and any future procurement strategy. Lot 1: . Please see the attached documentation for further information and details of the documents to be returned by interested suppliers. Responses will be reviewed by the University to inform its understanding of the current market, available technologies and delivery approaches. The information provided will support longer-term planning, strategic planning and, where appropriate, any future procurement strategy. This Prior Information Notice (PIN) is issued solely for the purpose of preliminary market engagement. It is not a call for competition and should not be interpreted as a commitment to undertake a procurement exercise or award any contract. Should a procurement be taken forward, it is anticipated that this could take place at any point within the next three to five years. The University welcome participation from all interested suppliers. Participation is voluntary, at each suppliers’ own cost and will not affect any future procurement process.. Interested suppliers should send the requested information to Suzanne Toole, Procurement Manager, suzie.toole@ed.ac.uk by 12 Noon (BST) on 04 September 2026. Suppliers should mark their email with ‘PIN Response “SUPPLIER NAME”– Student Record Platform’.

This procurement is conducted in accordance with the Public Procurement Act (2016:1145) (LOU). result.text: The purpose of this request for information is to clarify questions, obtain information and preliminary cost estimates related to a comprehensive digital pathology solution to be deployed by Fimlab Laboratoriot Oy (hereinafter “Fimlab” or "Contracting Entity"). This is not a Call for Tenders, but a market consultation; request of information. Fimlab invites interested suppliers to participate in the market consultation and requests their views regarding the planned procurement. The Contracting Entity is not committed to carrying out the procurement referred to in this request for information. Decisions on whether to initiate a possible procurement process will be made after the market consultation. SUBJECT OF THE PROCUREMENT The subject of the procurement is more detailed in annexes. Through this request for information, Fimlab seeks, among other things, to determine to assess the level of documentation and requirements, as well as market trends. RESPONDING TO THE REQUEST FOR INFORMATION Please respond to the questions and to submit the completed attachment via the Supplier Portal. The responses will be used in the preparation of the procurement and in the finalization of the Call for Tenders and its appendices. All responses will be treated confidentially. Information will not be disclosed to other suppliers without written consent for such disclosure. Responses may be submitted in Finnish or English in freeform written format. Respondents are requested to follow the numbering of the questions and to clearly indicate any trade secrets or confidential information. Responding to this request for information will not affect the position of a potential tenderer in any subsequent tender procedure. No remuneration will be paid for participation in the request for information. At this stage, the market consultation is being conducted solely through written submissions. However, the Contracting Entity may, at its discretion, invite participants to further discussions if clarification of the responses or additional information is considered necessary. In this case, the Contracting Entity, may continue supplier-specific discussions with a maximum of 3 suppliers.

result.text: The MoJ is currently exploring the future of intermediary services provision and conducting preliminary market engagement, prior to any procurement process. This notice is published for transparency purposes in accordance with the Procurement Act (2023) and does not constitute the commencement of a procurement. The MoJ is exploring how these services may be delivered across the Ministry and the wider justice sector. Services being considered include those currently provided under the HMCTS Appointed Intermediary Services Frameworks (HAIS) and the Witness Intermediary Scheme (WIS), in addition to ad hoc intermediary services provided to support His Majesty's Prison and Probation Service (HMPPS) and the Parole Board. You can find out more about the current HAIS arrangements at: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/hmcts-intermediary-services#about-hmcts-intermediary-services You can find out more about the current Witness Intermediary Scheme at: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/ministry-of-justice-witness-intermediary-scheme Intermediaries are impartial communication specialists whose primary responsibility is to enable complete, coherent and accurate communication with vulnerable witnesses, defendants and parties in the justice system, in order to improve the quality of evidence and facilitate the vulnerable person’s understanding and participation in the proceedings. The role of an intermediary includes making an assessment and reporting, orally or in writing, about the communication needs of the vulnerable person and the steps that should be taken to meet those needs. It also includes implementing those measures, at a court hearing or interview, for example at a solicitor’s office or police station. Lot 1: . None

rejected.text: Tenderers are hereby invited to a market dialogue in connection with the procurement of an electronic board for FACT for health companies in the Helse Sør-Øst region. The market dialogue is part of the preliminary work for the procurement and is being carried out because the Contracting Authority would like input for the procurement from potential suppliers, and possibly also from other interested parties. As part of this process, suppliers are invited to provide input to the procurement prior to the announcement. The Contracting Authority requests written input on as many of the following points as possible: Short presentation of the interested party: Description of experience with the Fact Board. What does the tenderer consider to be its core activity and main competence? Tenderers are requested to provide a short description of customers who currently use the system, including, if possible, which parts of the system are used and for which user groups. Points we would like feedback on: Provide a description of the tenderer's system and how this covers the needs/purposes described. What are the main features and advantages? What type of delivery model/operational model can be provided (SaaS, other)? Does the tenderer have input on how any environmental requirements can be set for the system? Price models: Which price models does the tenderer operate with and what price models does the supplier recommend? Can the supplier comply with other models if the Contracting Authority deems it appropriate? What factors affect the price of the tenderer's system? Quality and security: What requirements does the tenderer have in relation to the quality of the system? What measures does the tenderer have to ensure that information security and privacy are safeguarded, with particular focus on sensitive areas such as patient safety? Where is the solution installed? Where are the personnel operating and maintaining the system? What kind of support and training does the service provider offer to ensure users get the most out of their solution? Which support and maintenance services does the tenderer offer? Other: How does the supplier work on innovation and further development of the product? How does the supplier ensure that the systems remain relevant in line with technological developments in the market? Are there special developments in the market that the Contracting Authority ought to take into consideration in designing a future-oriented agreement? Which SSA templates does the tenderer think are best suited for the delivery and why? Are there any other elements that the Contracting Authority should pay particular attention to? What should, in the tenderer's view, be emphasised in any future procurement? Furthermore, it may be of interest, if relevant for the interested party, to hear about the tenderer's experience from similar public tenders, possibly in comparable countries (preferably countries within the EU). Deadline for written feedback from interested parties: 19.11.2025 This is only a prior information notice to obtain information on the market and to have a dialogue with relevant suppliers. The actual competition may be announced at a later date. Sykehusinnkjøp HF is assisting Sykehuspartner HF and HSØ with the implementation of the market dialogue. See www.sykehuspartner.no and www.helse-sorost.no. For further information about the Contracting Authority, please register or submit questions about the market survey in the Mercell communication module. After this market survey, the Contracting Authority will assess the need to hold meeting(s) with relevant interested parties.
